title: I. Object-oriented programming (OOP): design and analysis

topics.title: A. Encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism
topics.coverage: Class-writing FRQs support constructors, encapsulation, and methods. Interface, inheritance, and Collectable examples extend this into polymorphic design.
topics.gap: Strengthen the connection between isolated class exercises and a tested, multi-class Web feature.
topics.pbl: Observe a Spring entity and controller, then extend the model without exposing internal state.

topics.title: B. Abstract classes and generics or parameterized types
topics.coverage: The abstract Fibonacci and Collectable lessons demonstrate abstract parents, interfaces, and typed collections.
topics.gap: Add a focused student-authored generic class exercise; using ArrayList<T> alone does not demonstrate designing a parameterized type.
topics.pbl: Extend a shared Collectable abstraction and explain the type contract used by its collection.

title: II. Software engineering design: techniques and strategies

topics.title: A. Memory management and garbage collection
topics.coverage: Stack and heap memory, reference types, and object-copying notes provide the foundation.
topics.gap: Finish the copying/memory draft with reachability, garbage collection, and object-lifetime checks.
topics.pbl: Trace references held by a controller or collection and explain when an object becomes eligible for garbage collection.

topics.title: B. Visibility, scope, binding, and lifetime
topics.coverage: Data types, reference semantics, POJOs, and class-writing practice support field visibility and local-versus-instance state.
topics.gap: Make scope, dynamic method binding, and lifetime explicit in a short comparative exercise.
topics.pbl: Compare request-local variables with entity fields and inspect an overridden method's runtime behavior.

topics.title: A. Copy constructors
topics.coverage: Reference and memory lessons are prerequisites; a dedicated object-copying skeleton exists.
topics.gap: The copy-constructor lesson is unfinished. Require shallow/deep-copy tests rather than treating reference assignment as copying.
topics.pbl: Create an independent snapshot of project data and verify that editing the original does not change the snapshot.

topics.title: B. Advanced input/output techniques - 1. Text and binary files
topics.coverage: JPA and backend references provide persistence context, but database persistence is not a substitute for file I/O.
topics.gap: Finish a text/binary import-export exercise with resource closure and round-trip tests.
topics.pbl: Add an export/import layer to a project collection and compare text and binary representations.

topics.title: B. Advanced input/output techniques - 2. Random access files
topics.coverage: The reliable-file-persistence draft includes fixed-size records and RandomAccessFile offsets.
topics.gap: No completed dedicated random-access file lesson is available in this collection.
topics.pbl: Update one fixed-size record by its offset without reading or rewriting every record.

topics.title: C. Recursive methods
topics.coverage: The Fibonacci lesson supplies an algorithm-comparison context. Methods/control practice supports the prerequisite method-writing skills.
topics.gap: Add explicit base-case, recursive-step, and call-trace checks; ordinary loops and method-writing FRQs alone do not cover recursion.
topics.pbl: Compare recursive and iterative implementations, then explain the call-stack cost.

topics.title: D. Fault-tolerance through exception and error handling
topics.coverage: Backend and file-persistence materials provide contexts for invalid input, persistence failures, and recovery.
topics.gap: Finish a dedicated exercise that tests failure paths, useful error reporting, and safe resource handling.
topics.pbl: Send invalid input or a malformed import to a project feature and verify the reported error and unchanged valid data.

topics.title: A. ArrayLists, vectors, linked lists, and iterators
topics.coverage: Collection/list lessons and array-processing FRQs provide traversal, modification, and iteration practice. The 2D example is supporting array practice, not a separate CS112 outline section.
topics.gap: Finish the from-scratch LinkedList layers and explicitly compare Vector with ArrayList. Library usage is not a custom implementation.
topics.pbl: Build a small review queue using student-authored nodes, insertion, and traversal, with empty and singleton tests.

topics.title: B. Data structure assessment and appropriate selection
topics.coverage: Collection introductions, summaries, Comparable, and queue references support choosing structures for project needs.
topics.gap: Require students to justify their selection using actual operations and test data. Deeper sort analysis belongs to the CS113 extension.
topics.pbl: Compare a list and a map for a project's lookup needs, then justify the chosen structure.

topics.title: A. Graphical user interface (GUI) design
topics.coverage: Fullstack design, frontend UI, Thymeleaf, and concrete viewer/game examples support browser-based GUI design.
topics.gap: Strengthen accessibility, validation, and user-flow evaluation in student project evidence.
topics.pbl: Evaluate a form or table with a user, then improve its feedback and keyboard interaction.

topics.title: B. Java applets or Web
topics.coverage: Use the Web pathway: Spring-backed pages, frontend/backend integration, JQuery, and generated CRUD tables. Applets are not the teaching target.
topics.gap: Require an end-to-end feature with a clear API contract and demonstrated success and error states.
topics.pbl: Connect a browser interaction to a Spring endpoint and persist or retrieve project data.

topics.title: Individual and group hands-on projects
topics.coverage: Projects support, complement, and extend lecture material and theory. Existing feature documentation provides examples to observe and extend, not proof that students have implemented the underlying CS112 concepts.
topics.gap: Collect individual competence evidence alongside group project work, followed by summative evaluation and reflection.
topics.pbl: Choose a feature, identify its CS112 concepts, implement an extension, demonstrate it, and reflect on test evidence.
